nodes.label: graphify Skill (OpenCode)
nodes.rationale: Packages the whole graphify pipeline as an agent skill so any folder of code/docs/papers/images becomes a persistent, queryable knowledge graph with an honest EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS audit trail.

nodes.label: Fast Path - Existing Graph
nodes.rationale: If graph.json already exists and the request is a natural-language question, rebuilding wastes tokens and time — jump straight to query instead of re-detecting and re-extracting.
nodes.source_location: What You Must Do When Invoked

nodes.label: Step 1 - Ensure graphify Installed / Resolve Interpreter
nodes.rationale: Interpreter is resolved once (uv tool, then shebang, then python3) and persisted to .graphify_python so every later block uses the same environment across invocations.

nodes.label: Step 2 - Detect Files
nodes.rationale: Sidecar is written from Python rather than a shell redirect so the block renders identically on PowerShell hosts without console-encoding drift (#2528).

nodes.label: Step 2.5 - Video/Audio Transcription
nodes.rationale: Video/audio is transcribed to text first so downstream semantic extraction can treat transcripts as ordinary doc files.

nodes.label: Step 3 - Extract Entities and Relationships
nodes.rationale: Splits deterministic free AST work from token-costing LLM work, and runs both in parallel because they operate on disjoint file types (saves 5-15s on large corpora).

nodes.label: No-API-Key Policy
nodes.rationale: Code extraction is AST-only so a code-only corpus needs no key at all; semantic extraction uses Gemini only if GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY is already set, otherwise the host agent is itself the LLM — prompting for a provider key is a misread of the skill.

nodes.label: Part A - Structural (AST) Extraction
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and free, so it is started immediately and in parallel with the semantic subagents.

nodes.label: Part B - Semantic Extraction via Parallel Subagents
nodes.rationale: Only docs, papers, and images need an LLM; a code-only corpus writes an empty semantic file instead so Part C's unconditional read never hits FileNotFoundError.

nodes.label: Step B0 - Semantic Cache Check
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are attributed to the extraction-spec prompt file so a graphify upgrade that changes the prompt forces re-extraction while an unchanged prompt keeps its entries (#1939); the cached sidecar is deleted when empty so Part C never merges stale results (#1392).

nodes.label: Step B1 - Split Into Chunks
nodes.rationale: Chunks of 20-25 files group same-directory files together so cross-file relationships are more likely to be extracted; each image gets its own chunk because vision needs separate context.

nodes.label: Step B2 - @mention Parallel Dispatch (OpenCode)
nodes.rationale: OpenCode has no Agent tool, so subagents are dispatched via @mention; all mentions in a single message run in parallel, with a serial chunk-file fallback if @agent cannot write files.

nodes.label: Step B3 - Collect, Cache, and Merge Chunks
nodes.rationale: Chunk file presence on disk is the success signal; a missing file means the subagent was likely read-only, and more than half missing aborts because the graph would be silently incomplete. Real token counts come from the Agent result usage field since chunk JSON carries placeholder zeros.

nodes.label: Part C - Merge AST + Semantic Extraction
nodes.rationale: AST nodes are kept first and semantic nodes deduplicated by id, so deterministic structural facts win over LLM-inferred duplicates.

nodes.label: Step 4 - Build, Cluster, Analyze, Generate Outputs
nodes.rationale: Empty-graph guard runs before any write so a failed extraction cannot clobber a good graph.json or report (#1392); export happens first and the report is only written when to_json actually wrote, so docs never describe a graph on disk that does not exist.

nodes.label: Shrink Guard (#479)
nodes.rationale: to_json refuses to write when the new graph has fewer nodes than the existing graph.json, so a partial run cannot silently shrink an accumulated graph; an intentional shrink requires an explicit --force full rebuild.

nodes.label: IS_DIRECTED Build Option
nodes.rationale: --directed builds a DiGraph preserving source->target edge direction; the default is an undirected Graph.

nodes.label: Step 4.5 - Graph Health Check
nodes.rationale: Read-only and never aborts, because dangling/missing endpoints, self-loops and collapsed edges are the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches — the graph stays usable but the issue must be visible per the Honesty Rules.

nodes.label: Step 5 - Label Communities
nodes.rationale: Questions are regenerated after labeling because labels affect question phrasing, and graph.json is re-exported so nodes carry the curated community_name (#2490).

nodes.label: Step 6 - HTML and Obsidian Export
nodes.rationale: HTML is always generated unless --no-viz; the Obsidian vault is opt-in because it writes one file per node.

nodes.label: Step 9 - Manifest, Cost Tracker, Cleanup, Report
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that actually produced output are stamped, so a failed chunk stays unstamped and is re-queued next --update instead of being marked done and lost forever (#2015); manifest keys are relativized to the scan root for portability across clones (#1417).

nodes.label: Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge, never hide cohesion behind symbols, always show token cost — the audit trail is the product, so uncertainty is labelled AMBIGUOUS rather than dropped.

nodes.label: Interpreter Guard for Subcommands
nodes.rationale: Re-resolves the interpreter when .graphify_python is missing, e.g. after the user deletes graphify-out/.

nodes.label: /graphify query Flow
nodes.rationale: The question is expanded against the graph's own vocabulary first so a wording mismatch does not collapse the answer to noise; answers cite source_location and fall back to inline NetworkX traversal if the CLI is unavailable.

nodes.label: graphify.llm.extract_corpus_parallel
nodes.rationale: Used instead of subagent dispatch when a Gemini key is present; default model gemini-3-flash-preview, overridable via GRAPHIFY_GEMINI_MODEL or --model.

nodes.label: graphify.build.build_from_json
nodes.rationale: root= relativizes source_file to the same base as the --update runbook so full builds and incremental updates never drift apart on node keys (#1361).

nodes.label: graphify.detect.save_manifest
nodes.rationale: scan_corpus is the raw full corpus, not the stamp-filtered subset, so newly excluded in-root files are dropped rather than masquerading as deletions (#1908).

nodes.label: references/extraction-spec.md
nodes.rationale: Doubles as the cache key: entries are stamped with the prompt that produced them, so read and write must pass the same SPEC_PATH (#1939).

nodes.label: graphify Skill (Trae)
nodes.rationale: Same pipeline as the OpenCode skill, re-targeted at the Trae host whose only difference is the subagent dispatch mechanism.

nodes.label: Step B2 - Task Tool Parallel Dispatch (Trae)
nodes.rationale: Trae exposes a Task tool for parallel subagents; all Task calls go in one response so they run in parallel, and the extraction prompt is passed as the task description.

nodes.label: Absolute CHUNK_PATH Derivation
nodes.rationale: PROJECT_ROOT is cwd — where Part C globs graphify-out/ — not .graphify_root or the scan dir, otherwise chunk files land where the merge never looks (#1392).
nodes.source_location: CHUNK_PATH must be an absolute path

nodes.label: Trae Has No PreToolUse Hooks
nodes.rationale: AGENTS.md rules serve as the always-on enforcement mechanism in place of PreToolUse hooks.
